findings.severity: major on Python 3.10, the README's stated minimum (no effect on 3.11 and later)
findings.claim: time_coverage_start and time_coverage_end carry one fraction digit (2026-10-17T15:58:55.9Z); datetime.fromisoformat cannot read it before Python 3.11.
findings.change: _iso_utc(text) reads the ISO UTC text with a regex and strptime, with one fraction digit, several, or none. read_cmip uses it in place of fromisoformat. The README's Python minimum is unchanged. Tests: test_a_file_scan_time_reads_with_one_fraction_digit_none_or_six (the helper, including a bad string) and test_a_file_whose_scan_end_has_no_fraction_or_six_digits_is_read (through read_cmip; the one-digit case is the existing read test).
findings.evidence: On Python 3.10.20, datetime.fromisoformat('2026-10-17T15:58:55.9+00:00') raises ValueError (Invalid isoformat string). With the old parse reinstated in a scratch copy, the satellite tests on 3.10 fail five ReadFile tests (one failure, four errors). With the fix, the six website test modules pass on 3.10 (319 tests), 3.12 (319 tests) and 3.13 (363 tests in the full discovery).

findings.claim: GOES-West was tried only when GOES-East's listing, download or decode failed, and a GOES-West picture after an East failure was not ok. An East scan older than the hour gave no picture and no West attempt.
findings.change: (1) _newest raises _NoScan when East lists no scan, or its newest scan is older than UNAVAILABLE (60 minutes); _live then tries GOES-West. (2) A GOES-West picture is ok by freshness alone, like an East picture. Its status detail names the East reason in brackets, for example 'scan ended 9:58 am (GOES-West; GOES-East file list didn't load (HTTP 503))'. Reason strings now begin with the satellite's name and drop the leading 'the', to match that example. With no picture, the detail is 'no satellite scan in the last 60 minutes' when no satellite has a scan; otherwise each satellite's reason is named. Tests updated: test_east_listing_failing_draws_west_and_says_so, test_east_download_failing_draws_west, test_east_file_that_does_not_decode_draws_west, test_a_picture_with_no_usable_value_is_a_failed_file, test_both_failing_names_both, test_east_failing_and_no_west_scan_names_both_reasons, test_a_fetcher_that_raises_is_a_status_and_never_a_crash, test_a_listing_that_fails_is_named_and_raised, test_no_scan_in_the_last_hour_draws_no_picture (now also checks that GOES-West was asked), test_the_west_picture_is_drawn_north_east_and_says_why, test_a_live_picture_is_described_in_plain_words. The old test test_an_old_east_scan_does_not_fall_back_to_west became test_an_east_scan_older_than_the_hour_falls_back_to_a_fresh_west_scan. Added: test_an_east_listing_with_no_scan_falls_back_to_west, test_a_west_picture_after_an_east_failure_goes_stale_like_an_east_one, test_a_stale_west_picture_after_an_east_failure_says_both_and_is_not_an_all_clear.
findings.evidence: Printed status for each case: East fresh; East list fails with West fresh, or with West 25 minutes old; East download fails; East has no scan with West fresh; East 61 minutes old with West 5 minutes old; East old with no West; no files; both lists fail; each one-sided failure. Mutant M3 (break instead of continue when a satellite has no scan) fails 3 tests. Mutant M4 (the old ok rule) fails 5 tests.

findings.change: describe() now reads: 'A cloud top 2 km up is drawn about 3 to 4 km north-west of its true place, and a top 12 to 15 km up about 20 to 33 km (parallax).' The direction is north-east for GOES-West. The tests assert the new sentence and that 'more for higher tops' is gone.

findings.claim: The wording said 'over Montana', 'how bright the cloud tops are', had no uncoloured sentence, and DESIGN said warm surfaces (290 K and above) are faded out.
findings.change: About: 'of the newest 5-minute scan over the map's area'; 'It is an observation of the infrared brightness temperature of the cloud tops and of the ground where there is no cloud'; 'Areas warmer than 300 K are left uncoloured, and missing areas show hatch lines; uncoloured is not a statement about the weather.' DESIGN: 'warm surfaces fade from 275 K, are faint at 290 K and are transparent from 300 K, so the basemap shows through.' describe() carries the uncoloured sentence, so the noscript panel and the List share one text.
findings.consequence: The About bullet, sources.CONTRACTS['satellite'].request and DECISIONS.md said GOES-West is used only if East fails. They now say East fails or has no scan in the last hour (finding C).

contradictions_with_the_decisions.claim: 43.7358 N 101.0125 W falls at column 2517, off the 2500-column grid.
contradictions_with_the_decisions.fact: It falls at column 2500 (unrounded 2499.66), one past the last column. Column 2517 belongs to 43.0 N 101.0 W, the brief's south-east corner. Both points are NaN.
contradictions_with_the_decisions.action: The test asserts NaN at 43.7358 N 101.0125 W with its true column (2500), and NaN at 43.0 N 101.0 W with column 2517. The supervisor should confirm the wording.

contradictions_with_the_decisions.claim: 42.811 N 117.182 W is a far-side point for GOES-East, so it is NaN only because of the visibility rule.
contradictions_with_the_decisions.fact: It is visible from GOES-East (visible True; scan angles x -0.080654 and y 0.110991 rad; column 369, row 308, inside the grid), so it is drawn at a finite value. It is also visible from GOES-West (column 1996, row 259). Neither satellite sees it as far side.
contradictions_with_the_decisions.action: Not used as the far-side point. The far-side test uses 50.0 N 151.5 W, found by search: not visible from GOES-East, inside the grid bounds, and drawn when the horizon rule is switched off. The named point is kept in a test that asserts it is visible and drawn. The supervisor should confirm this substitute.
